description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-03) from the BA (#1028) merge-review probe battery (scratchpad p1028/bit.pl row 20).  PRE-EXISTING; #1028's classifier documents it as "perl's false reaches here as the STRING """.

    print +((1==0) | "abc");   # perl: 0     -- PL_sv_no is a DUALVAR ("" and IV 0, NIOK set) so the op is NUMERIC
                               # PCL:  abc   -- PCL's false is the plain string "", so the op is the bit-STRING op
    print +((1==1) | "abc");   # perl: 1, PCL: 1 (CL T is classified :number -- right)

THE REPRESENTATION: PCL spells perl's FALSE as "" (p-bool answers 1 / ""), which is right for every stringy and truthy consumer and wrong for every consumer that asks "does this value CARRY A NUMBER" -- today only the bitwise mode decision (`%p-bitwise-operand-kind`), but the same question underlies `use warnings` numeric-vs-string diagnostics (#221) and any future NIOK-keyed rule.  A `!1` / `!!0` / failed comparison result is the commonest false there is, so `$flag | $mask` with a comparison-derived $flag silently takes the string op.
FIX SHAPE (decide first): (a) a distinguished false constant (a dualvar box "" / 0, the way `$!` is a dualvar -- `%pcl-dualvar-p` exists since #964) returned by every comparison and `!`, classified :number by the bitwise dispatch and "" by to-string -- touches p-bool and every comparison emitter, measure the bench (comparisons are hot; the raw-numeric regime returns raw 1 / nil?  check what the raw path returns for false: if it is CL NIL then NIL is ALSO "false" in raw slots and #1028 classes NIL as :string -- probe `my $f = (1==0); print $f | "abc"` on both PCL_OPT paths); or (b) leave the representation and special-case nothing -- document in not-supported.md as a known divergence with this reproducer.  (b) is a write-off of a silent wrong; prefer (a) if the bench allows, else (b) with the entry.
RELATED: #1028 (done), #1040, #221.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, representation): perl's FALSE is a DUALVAR (PL_sv_no: "" and IV 0, NIOK set) but PCL's is the plain string "", so every rule that asks "does the value carry a number" diverges -- `(1==0) | "abc"` is 0 in perl (numeric op) and "abc" in PCL (bit-string op); #1028's classifier documents the gap
